concepts.def: Random motion of particles in fluids

walkthroughs.h2: Brownian motion and evidence for particles
walkthroughs.body_html:
Brownian motion shows particles are moving randomly.

Smoke under a microscope jiggles due to air molecules.

Heating raises internal energy.

If only kinetic rises: temperature goes up.

If only potential rises: state changes.

Decrease volume -> more collisions per second -> higher pressure.

Increase temperature -> particles move faster -> higher pressure (at constant V).

mcqs.q: Reducing volume of gas at constant T leads to:
At room temperature and pressure, what volume does 1 mole of any gas occupy?
options: Heavier gases occupy a smaller volume per mole because their particles are denser.
Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.
Protons move from chlorine to sodium to balance the charges.
Approximately 24 dm^3 (24,000 cm^3), regardless of the identity of the gas.

mcqs.q: What happens to electrons when sodium reacts with chlorine?
options: Protons move from chlorine to sodium to balance the charges.
Sodium loses one electron to chlorine; the resulting Na+ and Cl- ions attract electrostatically.
Sodium and chlorine share an electron between them.
The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.

mcqs.q: In an exothermic reaction, what happens energetically with the bonds?
options: The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.
Bond breaking releases energy and bond making absorbs energy.
Energy released forming new bonds exceeds energy absorbed breaking existing bonds.
